ownerFeedback.quote: Thanks. I can see the variety and it's good we're able to introduce them, but I will note that this is clearly still only the beginning. That's not even to mention that the serpentine is kinda useless here because the rider kinda avoid the sepentine-y part of the right by bouncing it off
ownerFeedback.interpretation: Variety is encouraging; the serpentine riding experience remains inadequate in the reviewed example. No song or exact support was specified by the owner. The examples below are independently located illustrations, not an attribution of which moment the owner watched.

correction: Any contact with a displaced main segment includes glancing hits and isolated endpoint contacts. The historical 74/78 count does not establish traversal or a successful serpentine riding experience.

inspection.interpretation: Actual contacts with main segments displaced by the profile, relative to the same controls and incoming state at zero strength. Any-contact counts include glancing hits and do not establish traversal or useful riding. Timeline frames run at 40 fps; omitted frames have no collision with either rail of this support. Main segment zero is the approach. profilePhase is the segment midpoint in the construction heading schedule (null before its start), not rider time, arclength or a traversal score. Contacts include all rider points; simultaneous contacts do not establish ordering within a frame or continuous sliding. Guide IDs remain separate. This does not prove necessity or validate the zero-strength counterfactual ride.

checks: Every replay collision hash matches its saved cell.
Every actual main rail reconstructs exactly from its saved incoming state and controls.
Every original per-track and per-support field matches the v1 inspection.
Contact timeline frames are unique and ordered; main and guide frame counts match the original counts.

examples.description: Profile start contacted at frame 328, no line collisions on frames 329–333, then contact near profile end at frame 334. No guide contact on this support.
Maximum contacted profile midpoint phase 0.046819467474874005; last main contact frame 1005 on pre-profile entry; no guide contact, and no line collision on frames 1006–1019.

limitations: Construction phase is not arclength or a traversal score.
Collision IDs include any rider point; consecutive collisions do not prove continuous sled sliding.
These examples do not characterize every serpentine support or establish a geometry ceiling.
No compiler, targets, benchmark, detector, scorer or physics changed.
nextExperiment: Demonstrate one passage where the rider visibly follows the distinctive serpentine bends; compare profile placement and curvature within available contact time, then guide interaction, under unchanged musical targets. Inspect ordered collisions and finished video; preserve failures and measured costs.
